Assistance to Japanese Military Police re finding of alleged
Anti-Japanese papers in Grand Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road.

D.S. 207 Nicoll                                      Chief Inspector.

Sir,

    At 5.10.p.m. 4-5-38, a telephone message was received at
this Station from Inspector White, who, together with S.I. Lo
Ta Kung, J.P.C.s 141 and 161 (R.U.), C.P.C.s 1907, 2001, 2010,
2730, C.D.C.s 23, 149 and eight members of the Japanese Military
Police was carrying out a search party in the Grand Hotel, Yu Ya
Ching Road, to the effect that papers of an Anti-Japanese nature
had been found in Room 336 of the above Hotel.

    C.D.C.339 and the undersigned and later J.D.C. Kobayashi (C)
attended the scene. On enquiries at the scene being made it
was ascertained that the paper purporting to be of Anti-Japanese
nature had been found in an envelope on the dressing table by
one of the members of the Japanese Military Police. In a
leather suitcase was also found a miscellaneous collection of
papers and documents, these were thereupon placed in the suit-
case and brought to the Station for perusal.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE - 5 MAY 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）

    The Special Branch were informed of the affair and D.S.I.
Logan, S.I, together with two clerks attached to Special Branch
attended this Station when these papers and documents were
scrutinised, itemised and translations made. (Translations attach-
ed). Only one of these documents, a pamphlet, contained any
matter which might be considered in any way of an Anti-Japanese
character.

    Enquiries regarding the identity of the occupant of the
room revealed through the medium of the Register that the room
No.336 had been opened on 19-3-38 by one named Ngan Cheong Wah
(顏振華) et. Cantonese, paper merchant, and from the same day. It
was ascertained that this man had been a guest of a month ago by
another male Chinese whose address and name are not yet known.

1938年5月4日。

关于协助日本宪兵在虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）大华饭店查获涉嫌反日文件一事。

警佐 207号 尼科尔（Nicoll）                                      总督察。

先生：

    1938年5月4日下午5时10分，本分局接到怀特（White）督察的电话报告。当时，怀特督察与华籍高级探员罗达公（Lo Ta Kung）、华籍巡长141号和161号（俄籍队）、华籍巡捕1907、2001、2010、2730号、华籍便衣侦探23、149号以及八名日本宪兵正在虞洽卿路大华饭店执行搜查任务。电话称，在上述饭店的336号房间内发现了具有反日性质的文件。

    华籍便衣侦探339号及本人随后赶赴现场，日籍便衣侦探小林（Kobayashi）（华籍队）亦随后到达。经现场查询得知，所谓具有反日性质的文件，是由一名日本宪兵在梳妆台上的一个信封内发现的。此外，在一个皮箱内还发现了一批杂乱的纸张和文件，这些物品随即被装入皮箱并带回本分局审阅。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 - 1938年5月5日 特别科）

    特别科已获悉此事，特别科副督察洛根（Logan）、一名华籍高级探员以及两名特别科文员来到本分局，对这些文件和单据进行了仔细审查、逐项列出并作了翻译。（译文附后）。在这些文件中，只有一本小册子包含任何可被视为具有反日性质的内容。

    经查阅登记簿以查问房间住客的身份，查明336号房间于1938年3月19日由一名名为颜振华（Ngan Cheong Wah）的人开设，其为广东人，职业为纸商，并从当日起入住。经查实，此人在一个月前曾是另一名男性华人的客人，该男子的姓名和地址目前尚不清楚。

At the request of the person in charge of the Japanese

Later a message was received from C.D.C.82 to the effect

occupants of Room 336 and that the Japanese Military detectives
were also keeping observation on both rooms. C.D.C.339 and the
undersigned proceeded again to the Grand Hotel to investigate
this latest development, arriving at the hotel at 8.10.p.m.
and went direct to Room No.346, in which were C.D.C.82, J.P.C.
89 (C) and one plain cloth member of the Japanese Military
Police while another member was in the passage outside.
On making enquiries it was ascertained that the occupants
of Room 346 were three females named:-
(1) Tsung Tsang Sz (陳修氏) 31, Wenchow,
F/Female, residing above room.
(2) S Wang Sz (施汪氏) 26, Taichong,
F/Female, residing 18 Swatow Road
(a friend of the 1st named female).

应日本宪兵小队负责人的要求，留下了四名日本侦探在336号房间守候，以防任何住客返回，届时可在本分局警官的协助下对其进行审讯。鉴于此情况，已指派华籍便衣侦探82号留守，配合日本宪兵并提供必要协助，同时向本分局报告任何后续进展。
随后收到华籍便衣侦探82号的消息，称346号房间的住客与336号房间的住客有关联，且日本宪兵侦探也在同时对这两个房间进行监视。华籍便衣侦探339号及本人再次前往大华饭店调查这一最新情况，于晚上8时10分抵达饭店，直接前往346号房间。房内已有华籍便衣侦探82号、华籍巡长89号（华籍队）以及一名身着便服的日本宪兵，另有一名日本宪兵在房外走廊守候。

女/女，居住于楼上房间。

Nyen the occupant of room 336 and that to-night the girl ? Ah
Noen had been told to go and call Nyen in room 336 to come to
room 346 to join in the evening meal, although at this time
the man Tsung Wo Sung was not in room 346. This the girl did,
not knowing that the room was occupied by detectives. When
she walked into the room she was naturally questioned and the

The female Tsung on being questioned then, stated that she
expected her husband back very soon, thereupon C.D.C. 82, J. C.
89 and two of the Japanese Military stationed themselves in the
room leaving two of their number to observe room No.336. This
had taken place a short time previous to the undersigned and
C.D.C.339 attending. While questioning the females in Room
346 at 8.15.p.m. a male Chinese one Jung Au Ching (陳浩卿) 31,
Wenchow, M/paper Salesman, House No.4, Tuh Ming Li (德明里),
Rue Petit J.C. arrived at the room stating that he come to
visit his friend Tsung Wo Sung. He was detained and requested
to remain in Room 346, together with the detectives. At this
time the undersigned asked the Japanese Military detectives
if they wished to have the females handed over, they thereupon
stated that should the man Tsung Wo Sung return they did not
wish to detain the females, but failing his return, they would
request that the females be handed over but in the meantime
they would remain in the room to await the return of Tsung Wo
Sung. The undersigned and C.D.C.339 left, returning to the
Station.

The undersigned then informed Mr. Robertson D.C."A" as to
the developments in the case up to that time, and also informed

336号房间住客Nyen的朋友。今晚，女孩阿?（Ah Noen）被告知去336号房间叫Nyen来346号房间共进晚餐，尽管此时陈和生并不在346号房间。女孩照办了，她并不知道房间内有侦探。当她走进房间时，自然受到了盘问，从而自然地建立了两个房间之间的联系。
当时受讯问的陈姓女子表示，她预计丈夫很快回来，于是华籍便衣侦探82号、华籍巡长89号以及两名日本宪兵在房内驻守，留下两人监视336号房间。此事发生在本人及华籍便衣侦探339号到达前不久。晚上8时15分，当我们在346号房间讯问这几名女性时，一名男性华人陈浩卿（Jung Au Ching），31岁，温州人，男/纸商，住址为小西门路（Rue Petit J.C.）德明里4号，来到房间，声称是来拜访朋友陈和生。他被扣留，并被要求与侦探们一起留在346号房间。此时，本人询问日本宪兵侦探是否希望移交这几名女性，他们随即表示，如果陈和生回来，他们不希望扣留这些女性；但如果他不回来，他们将要求移交这些女性，但在此期间，他们将留在房间内等待陈和生归来。本人及华籍便衣侦探339号随即离开，返回分局。

随后，本人将案件截至当时的进展情况告知“A”区副总监罗伯逊（Robertson）先生，并告知

him of the wishes of the Japanese Military regarding the
females, with these wishes, Mr. Robertson stated that he was not
in favour.

Later at 10.25.p.m. the undersigned together with C.D.S.
274 again went to Room 346 of the Grand Hotel and told the
Japanese Military detectives that the females were to be taken
to the Station. They did not readily assent to this and
communicated with their Headquarters, however, the undersigned
asked the females if they would care to go to Louza Police
Station and on the situation being explained to them, they
readily assented, this was done, leaving C.D.S.s 88 and 136 to
render the Japanese any assistance which might be necessary.

As the undersigned was about to leave a roomboy one
Daung Zoong Ying (唐仲英) informed detectives that just after
8.p.m. and previous to the arrival of C.D.S.339 and the under-
signed two male Chinese had been taken away by two other
Japanese Military detectives who had been keeping Room 336 under
observation. The roomboy was brought to the Station to make a
statement, this development was immediately relayed to Mr.
Robertson and on his instructions it has been made the subject
of Misc. Report No.357/38.

Translation of a pamphlet. (MIMEOGRAPHED)
Found by Louza Police Search Party operating in conjunction with
Japanese Military Police Plain Clothes Party, in Room 335, Grand
Hotel, 4-5-38.

Dear brethren:-

    Since the fall of Nantungchow on March 17, the Japanese have
done all kinds of killing and raping. The people resident in the
district must be eyewitnesses of these outrages committed by the
invaders. We can no longer bear such sufferings. Therefore we
have fought our way back to Nantungchow. We think our all brethren
will be glad to hear of this news. We, however, wish to make some
demands of the people of that district.

    We recaptured Nantungchow with the assistance of a few hot
blooded comrades and we, therefore, are of the opinion that the
Japanese will plan to retake the city in the future. In order
to frustrate the attempt of the Japanese to retake the city, we
would request the people in the devastated district to cooperate
with us in resisting the Japanese and eliminating traitors and to
establish a mutual guarantee protection corps.

    We firmly believe that if we continue our best endeavours,
we are sure to achieve final victory.

                        The Political Department of the
                        Independent Company of the Special
                        Service Corps of the Peace
                        Preservation Corps Headquarters
                        (6th District) of Kiangsu Province.

1938年5月4日，由罗查警署搜查队与日本宪兵队便衣队联合行动，在大饭店335房间发现。

各位同胞：-

    自3月17日南通城陷落以来，日军进行了各种杀戮和强奸。居住在该区的人民必然是这些侵略者暴行的目击者。我们再也无法忍受这样的苦难。因此，我们已打回南通城。我想我们的全体同胞听到这个消息都会感到高兴。然而，我们要向该地区的人民提出一些要求。

    我们在几位热血同志的协助下收复了南通城，因此，我们认为日本人将来会计划重新夺回该城。为了挫败日本人重新夺回该城的企图，我们请求受灾地区的人民与我们合作，抵抗日本人并清除汉奸，并建立联保保护团。

    我们坚信，如果我们继续尽最大努力，我们一定会取得最终胜利。

                        江苏省保安司令部

Sir,
    I beg to report that between the hours of 3:10p.m. and 5:30
p.m. 4/5/34, I was in charge of a foot search-party consisting
of S.I.Lo Ta Kung, J.P.C.141 and J.F.C.163, C.P.C.s 1907, 2001;
2010 and 2730, C.D.C.s 23 and 149, together with 8 members of the
Japanese Military Police in civilian clothes.
    The party left Louza Station via Ningpo, Lloyd and Nanking Roads,
thence proceeded South on Yu Ya Ching Road, where searching of
vehicles and pedestrians actually commenced.
    While walking along Yu Ya Ching Road I asked J.P.C.163 if the
Military Police required the searching to be restricted to the
highways, or if they desired to visit and search hotels and
lodging houses. He enquired of the senior Japanese soldier
present and received a reply which was translated to me to the
effect that they would like to visit a hotel and/or lodging
house later. The party continued along Yu Ya Ching Rd. towards
Ave.Edward VII, searching passengers in rail-less trams and
other types of vehicles and pedestrians, and subsequently turned
East into Ave.Edward VII.
    On arrival of the party at the junction of Ave.Edward
VII and Yunnan Roads, I observed a large number of male Chinese
grouped together about 50 yards South on Yunnan Rd., whereupon
I instructed S.I.Loh Ta Kung and J.P.C.163 to proceed together
with 2 Chinese Constables to the junction of Yunnan and Pakhoi
Roads, via Kwangse Rd. and then both parties would close on the
group and search their persons. This manoeuvre was duly
accomplished and the suspects searched but nothing of an incrim-
inating nature was found on their respective persons.
    Subsequently the party proceeded West on Pakhoi Road

    搜查队经宁波路、 Lloyd路（今九江路附近）和南京路离开罗查分署，随后沿虞洽卿路向南行进，在此开始对车辆和行人进行实际搜查。
    在沿虞洽卿路行走时，我问印捕163号，宪兵队是否要求将搜查限制在主要道路上，还是希望视察并搜查旅馆和寄宿舍。他询问了在场的日本军曹，得到的答复翻译给我听，大意是他们稍后希望视察一家旅馆和/或寄宿舍。搜查队继续沿虞洽卿路向爱多亚路方向行进，搜查无轨电车和其他类型车辆中的乘客以及行人，随后向东转入爱多亚路。

May 13, 1938.                                      Morning Translation.

Standard and other local newspapers :-

THE DEATH OF A KUOMINTANG OFFICIAL IN SHANGHAI

On the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai
on August 13 last year, Chang Sung (張昇), a committeeman
of the former Shanghai Kuomintang Headquarters, was very
active in national salvation work. When the Chinese
troops withdrew from Shanghai, Chang went to Hankow but
later returned to Shanghai and continued his activities
in great secrecy. Soon afterwards he disappeared and
despite the efforts of his family nothing was heard of
him for several months.
Information has now been given out by certain
quarters that Chang had incurred the displeasure of a
certain party because of his national salvation activities
and had been carried off and tortured to make him disclose
the activities of the Kuomintang members in Shanghai.
Chang, however, refused to speak. His captors then
cut off all his fingers after which they put him to death.
Chang's body cannot be found.

上海一名国民党官员之死

去年8月13日上海战事爆发时，前上海国民党总部委员张昇（Chang Sung）在救国工作中非常活跃。当中国军队撤出上海时，张前往汉口，但后来返回上海，继续秘密进行活动。不久后他失踪了，尽管家人多方努力，数月内仍无任何消息。
现在有消息来源透露，张因其救国活动惹怒某一方，被绑架并遭受酷刑，逼其供出上海国民党成员的活动情况。
然而，张拒绝开口。随后，抓捕者切断了他所有的手指，之后将其杀害。
张的尸体至今未被找到。
